newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Five powers stage biggest exercise off Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Five powers stage biggest exercise off Malaysia.

text.p: Planes and warships from five countries staged the largest ever mock air and sea battles off the coast of Malaysia on Monday.

The 13-day exercise, codenamed Flying Fish '97, has been described as the most ambitious exercise in the history of the Five Power Defence Agreement (FPDA), the region's only multilateral defence pact involving outside powers.
The pact calls for Britain, Australia and New Zealand to consult on the defence of Singapore and Malaysia. All five are members of the Commonwealth.
The exercise involves 39 warships, including for the first time an aircraft carrier, and 160 jet fighters and transport carriers.
Britain is contributing much of the muscle. Its 16 ships included the aircraft carrier HMS Illustrious, three frigates and a support vessel, a British High Commission statement said.
Two thirds of Britain's 3,000-man force here are crew members of Illustrious.
The British naval contingent left home in January as part of Ocean Wave '97, which is visiting 34 countries and taking part in 26 exercises.
Ocean Wave is intended to show that Britain continues to have security interests in the region after it hands back Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30, British diplomats said.
Part of the British naval force will take part in a training exercise with the Royal Brunei Air Force after Flying Fish.
Britain said it plans to keep a Gurkha battalion in Brunei after the Hong Kong handover and is selling Brunei at least a dozen Hawk jet fighters and two frigate-class warships.
